verdicts.quote_a: 375,618 projections; 771.1 GB at verification (754 GB by du on 2026-09-25)
verdicts.quote_b: 808.615 GB on Ceph
verdicts.explanation: The atlas (17 Oct) gives 771.1 GB at fetch verification and 754 GB by du on 25 Sep; the registry (20 Oct) gives 808.615 GB on Ceph for the cobra2026 folder. The manifest (8 Oct) gives 771 GB in its source row and 809 GB for the COBRA2026 folder in its census, whose sizes it calls apparent bytes. The figures come from different measures (catalogued file sizes, du, apparent bytes of the whole folder), and no page reconciles them or says what else the folder holds.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry 692 cases and 375,618 projections, and give the size with its method: 771.1 GB at verification (atlas), 809 GB apparent bytes of the folder (manifest census, registry). A byte count of the projections against the whole cobra2026 folder would settle it.

verdicts.quote_a: Project adds two-labeller boxes on 150 Elekta exports and an LSTV screen of the 692 planning CTs (91 calls, unread).
verdicts.quote_b: all 467 cases on Ceph; 145 in a bank of 24 frames each, the rest never exported
verdicts.explanation: The atlas's annotation line says 150 Elekta exports, but its own notes say only 145 of 692 cases are in any frame bank, and its bank row gives cobra_elekta 3,480 frames (145 x 24). The registry says 145 are in the bank and the rest were never exported, which leaves no room for 150 exports. The 150 is not reconciled anywhere.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry 145 Elekta cases in the bank, 3,480 frames at 24 each, from the registry and the atlas's notes; flag the atlas's 150 exports as unreconciled.

verdicts.quote_a: C-ArmLSpine: 149 cases, 148 cases with 296 frames, or 120 distinct subjects.
verdicts.quote_b: 149 acquisition sessions (not provably one person each)
verdicts.explanation: The case counts agree once scoped: the release has 149 cases (sessions) in the atlas, the registry and the manifest. The atlas says 148 cases with 296 frames is the pre-repair bank, and that carm_drr covers 120 cases. How many people the 149 sessions are is open: the literature-state lists it among its unknowns, and the atlas says the sessions are not provably one person each.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry 149 cases (acquisition sessions) with the person count unknown. A person-level key from the release, or from its authors, would settle whether 149, 148 or 120 people are behind it.

verdicts.quote_b: unpacked 59,609 files, 23,347,039,978 B
verdicts.explanation: The registry gives 86.834 GB for C-ArmLSpine, with the grid path of the whole carmlspine folder. The atlas gives the Zenodo zip as 15,581,614,253 bytes and the unpacked tree as 23.3 GB, and puts derived banks, levels and poses under the same folder. Neither page says what the 86.8 GB counts, so it may be zip plus unpacked tree plus derived files, but no page says so.
verdicts.resolution_hint: For re-acquisition, carry the atlas's figures (zip 15.58 GB, unpacked 23.3 GB, 59,609 files). A du of the carmlspine folder broken down by subfolder would explain the registry's 86.834 GB.

verdicts.quote_a: 2 cases x 301 projections (602 in all; the case134 spin is counted as 302 frames in one document)
verdicts.quote_b: 301 XA frames each; rotational, not cranio-caudal
verdicts.explanation: The atlas and the registry agree: 301 frames per sweep and 602 in all, with the case134 bank at 301 items. The atlas names the 302 only as the count in one other document, and the research directions page carries that 302-frame spin. The two pages compared do not disagree.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry 301 frames per sweep, 602 projections, from the registry and the atlas; note that research directions says 302 for case134.

verdicts.quote_a: two labellers agreeing on 814 of 910 bodies
verdicts.quote_b: automatic truth agreeing on 814 of 910 vertebrae
verdicts.explanation: The registry says two labellers agreed on 814 of 910 bodies and never calls them people. verdicts.quote_a: "generated": "2026-09-14 09:43", "manifest_rows": 10281, "manifest_version": "1.1", "dataset_version": "0.2"
verdicts.quote_b: manifest 21,603 rows keyed by about 1,197-1,953 source documents (no patient key)

verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry 21,603 manifest rows with QC pending on all, from the atlas; give the card's 10,281 as the 14 Sep figure.

verdicts.quote_a: 316 GB; dropped from training, kept as a test set
verdicts.quote_b: still train on 2,632 VinDr crops and 2,100 FluoroCap crops per fold bank
verdicts.explanation: The manifest states the directive that drops FluoroCap from training. The handoff of the same day says the older C-ArmLSpine fold banks still hold FluoroCap crops, calls this a defect against that same directive, and says fold models without them already exist. The registry of 20 Oct carries both facts together. The pages describe a directive and a lagging defect, not two readings of one fact.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry the registry's wording: out of training by directive D1, a test set at most, still inside the old fold banks (the handoff's 2,100 FluoroCap crops per fold bank).

verdicts.quote_a: Two releases from one manifest: Dataset A (all open-access licence tiers, research use) and Dataset B (CC BY, CC0 and public-domain panels only).
verdicts.quote_b: Level-identification code, FluoroCap, model weights, spinesurg-ct-nnunet, XRSpinoPelvic1K. Never in a public repository, never on the website.
verdicts.explanation: The card (14 Sep) defines two releases, A and B, but never says they are public; it describes freezing them with a SHA256SUMS file. The lab recipe (27 Sep) puts FluoroCap among what stays private forever, and the atlas (17 Oct) says it is never redistributed. Whether the card's releases were meant to be public is not stated, so the texts do not show a planned public release being reversed.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry FluoroCap as private and never redistributed (lab recipe, atlas), with A and B as frozen internal subsets. The card's own release plan, or the protocol it names, would show whether public distribution was ever intended.

verdicts.quote_a: 17,075 index entries (9,667 cervical + 7,408 lumbar); 17,073 TIFF on disk (2 empty at the source)
verdicts.quote_b: 16,531 digitised films without landmarks
verdicts.explanation: The atlas gives 17,075 index entries and 17,073 TIFFs on disk. Its notes, like the registry, say 16,531 films are unannotated, and both give 543 landmarked films from the separate Zenodo set. 17,073 minus 543 is 16,530, one fewer than 16,531, and no page says whether all 543 landmarked films are among the 17,073 CDC films.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry 17,073 films on disk (atlas, board) and 543 landmarked (Zenodo). A count of the CDC TIFFs that have no Zenodo landmark entry would settle the 16,531.

verdicts.quote_a: (17,075 TIFFs, public domain, no registration)
verdicts.quote_b: No copyright bar; the DUA's "statistical reporting and analysis only" is a lawyer's question.
verdicts.explanation: The X-ray handoff of 3 Sep calls the full NHANES II set public domain with no registration. The board of 11 Sep, in a licence table it says was checked against primary sources, agrees there is no copyright bar but adds an NCHS data use agreement whose 'statistical reporting and analysis only' clause leaves commercial use unknown. The decisions page repeats 'NHANES if counsel agrees'. The later reading adds a term the handoff omitted.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry the board's reading: a federal work with no copyright bar, under an NCHS DUA whose commercial use waits on counsel; the Zenodo landmark set is separately CC BY 4.0.

verdicts.quote_a: VinDr-SpineXR is restricted. The page states: "Only registered users who sign the specified data use agreement can access the files."
verdicts.quote_b: VinDr-SpineXR requires a personal PhysioNet credentialed account — CITI training plus supervisor attestation, typically weeks.
verdicts.explanation: The handoff of 3 Sep says it corrects 'the earlier report', which described VinDr as needing PhysioNet credentialing with CITI training, supervisor sign-off and weeks. That is the field report's wording. The handoff quotes the PhysioNet page as restricted access: register, sign the DUA, same day. The field report is undated but is plainly the report the handoff corrects. The later registry and manifest call VinDr credentialed again.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry the handoff's quoted PhysioNet wording (restricted, DUA 1.5.0), and flag that the registry's and manifest's 'credentialed' contradicts it until the record page is read again.

verdicts.quote_a: on the grid under a PhysioNet data use agreement that sits outside IRB determination 2026-269 (its own determination pending)
verdicts.quote_b: outside WSU determination 2026-269, covered by its supplement HPR 2026-330 (notice 2026-09-29)
verdicts.explanation: The registry (rendered 20 Oct) says VinDr's own IRB determination is pending, citing DATASET_USAGE.md 2.2. The atlas (17 Oct) says VinDr is covered by supplement HPR 2026-330, with a notice dated 29 Sep 2026, before both pages. They disagree on one fact, and the atlas gives the determination number and date while the registry gives neither.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry the atlas's statement: covered by HPR 2026-330 (notice 2026-09-29), the supplement to 2026-269. The registry's 'pending' line should be corrected from that notice.

verdicts.quote_a: dropped from training; only implant boxes used
verdicts.quote_b: still train on 2,632 VinDr crops and 2,100 FluoroCap crops per fold bank
verdicts.explanation: The handoff of 8 Oct says the C-ArmLSpine fold banks still hold 2,632 VinDr crops per fold bank, while VinDr is 0 of 10,466 in the level bank. The lesion classes are given as 13 types (X-ray handoff) and 7 detectable classes (decisions), and the atlas itself calls 13 against 8 unreconciled.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry VinDr as out of the level bank and in the old fold banks as of 8 Oct (handoff). A listing of the current fold banks would settle whether it is still there, and a count from the release's annotation file would settle the classes.

verdicts.quote_a: 3,600 patients, 7,200 images (3,600 AP + 3,600 lateral); on disk AP 3,600 jpg + 3,600 csv, LA 3,604 jpg (three exact copies) + 3,606 csv
verdicts.quote_b: 3,603 lateral and 3,600 AP lumbar radiographs of 3,600 people
verdicts.explanation: The atlas separates its scopes: the release is 3,600 patients and 7,200 images; on disk there are 3,600 AP and 3,604 lateral jpg, three of them exact copies; and its notes say 3,603 lateral films are in the v9 bank. The registry's 3,603 lateral and 3,600 AP of 3,600 people fits the on-disk and bank counts, and the decisions page's 7,204 is the on-disk total. The literature-state's '3,600 films from 1,200 patients' is a reading the two compared pages do not carry.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry the atlas: release 3,600 patients and 7,200 images; on disk 7,204 jpg (lateral 3,604 including three exact copies); 3,603 laterals in the v9 bank.

verdicts.quote_a: the L4L6 sheet flags 129 four-lumbar and 15 six-lumbar cases
verdicts.quote_b: 3,461 normal / 15 lumbarization / 130 sacralization — 4.0% prevalence
verdicts.explanation: The atlas counts from the release's L4L6 sheet: 129 four-lumbar and 15 six-lumbar. The board counts from the S1a row's class field on lateral films: 15 lumbarization and 130 sacralization. Those two counts sum to 3,606, the atlas's lateral csv count, which includes duplicates. The fields and categories differ (four-lumbar against sacralization), so the one-case gap cannot be read as an error on either page.
verdicts.resolution_hint: A count from one field after removing the three duplicate lateral files would settle it. Until then, carry both counts with their source fields (L4L6 sheet 129 and 15; class field 130 and 15).

verdicts.quote_a: no weight trained on them leaves the grid until the owner has read the licence
verdicts.quote_b: BUU-LSPINE, whose EULA forbids redistribution
verdicts.explanation: The registry's 'unread by the owner' records that the owner has not personally read the licence, and attaches a rule to that. The manifest, the atlas ('EULA, No License Provided; acknowledgement required, no re-identification; never redistribute') and the board ('bespoke EULA') state the terms as recorded. One fact is whether the owner has read it and the other is what the EULA says, so the pages do not conflict.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry the terms from the atlas (EULA, no redistribution, acknowledgement required) together with the registry's note that the owner has not yet read the licence and that no weight leaves the grid until then.

verdicts.quote_a: Grid state verified 3 Sep 2026 over ssh: buu_v1 77 files / 43 MB; cm_spine 0 files; csxa 6 files (repo only, no images)
verdicts.quote_b: 24,815 named cervical vertebrae, zero unparsable files

The manifest records CSXA acquired 1 to 9 Sept and BUU on 9 Sept, and the atlas later lists IEEE 236 as held.

verdicts.quote_b: four candidate API endpoints all returned errors

verdicts.quote_a: "licence": "by request form"
verdicts.quote_b: The host domain no longer resolves. Treat as research-only until someone answers.

No page states licence terms, so 'by request form' and 'none found' answer different questions.

verdicts.quote_a: 714 jpg (494/204/16), 698 annotated, 3,250 boxes; about 500 are BUU persons
verdicts.quote_b: 716 lateral lumbar: 208 Honduran + 508 from BUU

The later file count replaces the 716, and the 208/508 split rests on the older total.

verdicts.quote_b: Only the 208 Honduran are independent of BUU, and they are the only genuine cross-site lateral lumbar test set in the project.

The atlas (17 Oct) says about 500 are BUU persons plus 12 VinDr studies, excluded by directive D6, and that 71 non-duplicate films were left out with no written reason. So the registry's 'no new person' conflicts with both other pages.

verdicts.quote_a: 909.55 MB zip
verdicts.quote_b: 236 films, 1.3 GB

The atlas gives the held set as 236 films and 1.3 GB without saying whether that is the extracted tree, so the sizes may measure different things. On the pseudo-label result, the atlas says the IEEE arm was refuted by about 19 points. The registry says the IEEE arm was refuted, and separately that NHANES unannotated pseudo-labels cut anomalous accuracy 20 points. Whether these are one experiment or two is not stated.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry the zip as 909.55 MB (handoff) and the held tree as 1.3 GB (atlas). The results catalog row for each pseudo-label arm would settle which source and which magnitude goes with which experiment.

The decisions page records that it was pulled anyway ('you made the call'), tagged research-track and marked revisit. The registry of 20 Oct shows it held, 20,000 films of 44 synthetic identities, all on train in the G3 split, licence not recorded.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry the registry's state (held, all on train, licence not recorded) and the decisions page's research-track tag; the board's advice is the earlier recommendation that was overridden.

verdicts.quote_b: Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.22139642
verdicts.explanation: Protocol 1 (15 Sep) cites zenodo.22642578, the handoff (8 Oct) cites zenodo.22139642, and the manifest names zenodo.22797014 as v11 (18 Sept), which the registry links. verdicts.quote_a: 1,228 and 1,935 scans with whole-body segmentation (the manifest counts v3 at 1,939)
verdicts.quote_b: 1,228 and 1,939 subjects

verdicts.resolution_hint: A count of L6 masks from the raw VerSe masks, the CT-3 step research directions names, would settle it; until then carry the four readings with their sources.

verdicts.quote_a: 2,293 vendor frames unused with no written criterion
verdicts.quote_b: 2,293 of 2,659 frames have no released pose (some carry the FTRAC fiducial and could be posed)

verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry both: 2,293 of 2,659 vendor frames have no released pose and some could be posed from the FTRAC fiducial (atlas), and no written criterion excludes them (registry).

verdicts.quote_a: 286 raw DICOM frames + 233 unreferenced raw + 118 processed; 3 CT series; 5,492 files, 4.15 GB (5,490 held)

verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry the atlas: 637 frames (286 raw, 233 unreferenced raw, 118 processed) in 5,490 held files, from five or six C-arms.

verdicts.quote_a: SchwingNet, data/sources, 60 records, rendered 2026-10-20

verdicts.quote_b: drafted 2026-09-23, not sent

verdicts.quote_b: The RSNA RATIC download link expires 2026-10-28 02:38 UTC.

VinDr-PCXR's grant on 21 Oct is an X-ray set and not one of the registry's gated CT rows.

verdicts.quote_a: a registration, not a letter; the count on the corpus page is to be checked when registering
verdicts.quote_b: 87 files, 19 GB on the grid; the scan counted about 53 adults, the UNM corpus page lists 7 participants

The atlas (17 Oct) gives it as held, 87 files and 19 GB, at that folder. The pipeline of 21 Oct says it is held in SchwingNet's record and fetched in spine-datasets.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry DysphagiaBank as held: 87 files, 19 GB (atlas, pipeline). The registry's reach should be corrected to held.

verdicts.quote_a: The only published collection of overlapping intraoperative C-arm frames of the spine, exactly the acquisition the sweep protocol simulates.
verdicts.quote_b: four pulsed fluoroscopy runs at 7.5 frames a second, the detector moved cranially along the spine during tilting: the only overlapping travelling frames found
verdicts.explanation: Each 'only' carries its own stated scope. SX-Stitch is the only published intraoperative collection, and it is not held (request only). The Bern myelography runs are the only overlapping travelling frames found that are public and on the grid, and they are not intraoperative. The atlas itself calls Bern the closest public case. The C-ArmLSpine sweeps are the only consecutive sequences with a paired volume, and they are rotational. The qualifiers make the three statements compatible.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry each with its qualifier: SX-Stitch (published, intraoperative, not held), Bern (public, travelling, held as re-encoded MP4s), C-ArmLSpine sweeps (paired volume, rotational).
